t: Maximum Sum of Almost Unique Subarray
o: Over all windows of length k containing at least m distinct values, maximize the window sum. Fixed-size sliding window with a frequency map: add the entering element, drop the leaving one, track distinct count and sum, and record the sum whenever distinct ≥ m. Example 1: window [2,6,7,3] has 4 distinct and sum 18, the answer.
k: Window size is fixed at k, so slide one step at a time updating a Counter in O(1).
Track (sum, distinct count) incrementally; a value becomes 'distinct lost' only when its count hits 0.

a.i: For each of the n−k+1 windows, recompute the set and sum directly. O(nk) — fine for n = 2e4 and small k, and the clearest baseline.
s: Slide a window of size k across nums.
For each window compute its sum and number of distinct elements.
Track the max sum among windows with distinct ≥ m; return 0 if none.
a.t: O(nk) — each window rebuilt from scratch

a.n: Approach 2: Sliding Window with Frequency Map
a.i: Maintain a Counter of the current window, its sum, and its distinct count. On each slide, increment the incoming value (new distinct if count goes 0→1), decrement the outgoing (lost distinct if count hits 0), adjust the sum, and update the answer when distinct ≥ m.
s: Build the first window's Counter, sum, distinct count.
For each subsequent position: add nums[i+k−1], remove nums[i−1], update sum/distinct, record if eligible.
Return the max (0 if never eligible).
a.t: O(n) — amortized O(1) per slide with hash map operations

w: Always present the sliding window as the real solution; brute force is only a sanity baseline. Pitfalls: deleting keys when counts hit zero (so Map.size reflects distinct count), and remembering the 0-if-none-exists return. Follow-up: variable window length, or 'exactly m distinct' instead of at least.
